subject: Short pilot: temporary capacity top-up, conversion path & pricing options
messages:
From: Cicely Marsh <cicely@lumenhealth.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Short pilot — can we top up capacity / extend?

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — things looked promising. We started pushing a slightly larger dataset through the short pilot and are hitting concurrency limits that are skewing our results. Two quick asks from our side:

1) Can we add temporary capacity (burst hours) for the remaining 10 days of the pilot to finish the workload?
2) If we do that, what are the conversion options to a committed plan afterwards (credits vs seat-based vs burst-run conversion)? Any pricing impact if we take a small discount for converting within 30 days?

We need to present options to our procurement team by next Tuesday. Appreciate a short options list + estimated costs.

— Cicely
Cicely Marsh
Head of ML Platform, LumenHealth
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Cicely Marsh <cicely@lumenhealth.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short pilot — can we top up capacity / extend?

Hi Cicely — thanks for the note and for running the larger dataset.

Quick summary of feasible options from our side: 

• Short burst (top-up): Add a one-time 72-hour burst pool (pre-provisioned GPU capacity). Pricing: $X,XXX for the pool + per-token runtime. No change to pilot end date; used capacity converts to credits if you convert to a commitment within 30 days.

• Short timebox extension: Add 14 extra days to the pilot with the same baseline capacity. Pricing: prorated pilot fee at 60% of standard daily rate. Extension preserves evaluation metrics and gives more time to prove ROI.

• Temporary Dedicated slice with conversion credit: Provision a small dedicated slice for the remainder of the pilot (higher per-hour cost) but if you sign a 3-month reserved commit within 30 days, we apply a conversion credit equal to 30% of the dedicated slice fees (applied to first invoice).

I'll loop David on throughput/latency impacts (he can confirm whether a burst pool addresses the concurrency profile you're seeing). If you want a small conversion incentive, I can check in with my manager for a limited promotional credit — it's likely feasible if we get procurement engaged quickly.

Deliverable: I'll send a short comparison matrix + an appendix with the burst configuration and estimated costs by EOD today. Would that timing work for you?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>
To: Cicely Marsh <cicely@lumenhealth.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short pilot — can we top up capacity / extend?

On Mon, Jun 15, 2026 at 08:37 Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> I'll loop David on throughput/latency impacts (he can confirm whether a burst pool addresses the concurrency profile you're seeing).

Cicely — quick technical note: the concurrency you're describing maps to a short-lived request spike pattern. A 72-hour burst pool configured with 8 concurrent worker slots and prefix/CACHE warm-up will likely eliminate the spike-related errors and give a representative burn-rate for peak hours. The attached appendix has the sizing assumptions I used.

Impacts to watch for: token-level costs will increase during burst windows; if you convert to a reserved commit and accept quantized runtime profiles, unit costs drop ~30% relative to the burst pool. We can model the exact numbers if you share a 3-day sample of the logs.

Attachment: burst-config-appendix.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — sizing table + warm-up instructions

— David
David Kim
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short pilot — can we top up capacity / extend?

Looping in from a commercial perspective. Neha — if LumenHealth signs a conversion to any committed tier within 30 days of pilot close, we can offer a one-time onboarding credit of up to 10% of the committed ARR (applied across the first two invoices). For the short burst / conversion credit combo, we can do: 

• 72-hour burst: standard burst fee; if converted within 30 days, apply 50% of the burst fee back as a billing credit + 10% onboarding credit on committed ARR.

This approval is limited to this quarter and contingent on Procurement/Legal timelines (we need a signed SOW/Order Form). Neha — please confirm that this promotional path is included in your options matrix.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial — Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Short pilot top-up — options matrix and next steps

Hi Cicely / Tom / Procurement team —

Attached is a short options matrix and the burst appendix (see attachments). Summary of the recommended path based on your timeline:

1) Immediate: Approve 72-hour burst pool (8 workers). Cost estimate: $4,200 (one-time) + runtime tokens. We will provision within 4 business hours of sign-off.
2) Evaluation: Use the burst hours to finish the data run and validate latency under load. David will help with warm-up steps.
3) Conversion: If LumenHealth signs a 3-month reserved commit within 30 days, Redwood will:
   • Apply a credit equal to 50% of the burst fee to your first invoice.
   • Provide a 10% onboarding credit off committed ARR across the first two invoices (as approved by Marissa).

Next steps: If this sounds good, Procurement can approve the burst PO and sign the short SOW. I've created a DocuSign envelope for the SOW: https://www.docusign.com/Signing/?r=doc123456789. Please reply-all with approval or any redlines by EOD Monday, Jun 22 so we can stay within fiscal quarter approvals.

Attachments: LumenHealth-MAP-v1.docx, burst-config-appendix.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Best,
